title: Understanding Confidence Intervals
text: A confidence interval gives a range of values that is likely to contain the population parameter with a certain level of confidence. In this case, a 95% confidence interval means that if we were to take many samples and construct a confidence interval from each sample, we expect 95% of those intervals to contain the true population mean.

title: Sample Mean vs. Population Mean
text: The statement refers to the sample mean, not the population mean. Remember, a confidence interval is constructed to estimate the population mean, not the sample mean.

title: Clarifying the Statement
text: The statement suggests that $$95$$ out of $$100$$ confidence intervals will include the sample mean. Is this true or false?
